rule: The words of the Handover, made at build time and read by the Unity host; nothing here is written live and no line decides anything (GDD §09: text is a light layer, history is what the systems record). The host finds a line with lookup() and picks a variant with pickIndex() (contracts/missions/handover/text.schema.ts): same seed and same run, same words. Keys follow the engine: verbs are the panel verb ids, outcomes the rulebook outcomes (`suspicious` when the person reports the approach), refusals are text codes found by lockOf() because the engine returns free text. People are named only Inez and Vale; everyone else is a role. Civilians are never the payload: no line asks a civilian to die, fight or be used as a weapon. Lines that name Halcyon are pending Sky (a Story proposal): ship the `unnamed` cliffhanger until Sky decides. Inez and the door guard are lovers (the Story spine; Sky, 2026-10-15): her debt is her need (Help), her secret is the guard (Pressure threatens to expose it). Written plainly and with tact, never explicit.

tone.world: An alternate 1950s that found atomic power centuries ago: 1950s manners and speech, centuries-ahead machines, no thinking machines or networks. Optimistic on the surface, coercive underneath: the city is polite, orderly and watching. Speech is plain, short and spoken; no period slang to dress it up, no modern internet speech.

voices.scout: energetic and chatty: quick, warm, short full sentences to her own cell; first to spot things and glad to say so; says plainly what is where and when; never wrong, never a joke to decode
voices.fixer: warm and persuasive: reassures, says "we", puts people at ease; steel under the kindness
voices.tech: calm and practical: procedure, minutes and what is tied to what; patient, a little dry about old wiring
voices.enforcer: dry, older, few words: one to four words where he can; gallows humour, never a speech
voices.waitress: Inez: warm café patter, quick, tired about money and the lender; her temperament shows in what she will and won't take
voices.driver: Popovic's official driver: gruff and practical; cars, wages, schedules; calls Popovic "the Councillor"
voices.guard: the door guard: officialese, clipped, the post and the rules; a mercenary one talks bonuses and "off the clock"
voices.councillor: Popovic: formal and pompous, then frightened; loyal blusters, mercenary bargains, fearful begs
voices.rivals: cold and businesslike: a contract, a schedule, no names
voices.patrol: a clockwork patrol: fixed polite phrases that mean orders ("Walking is encouraged. Running is noted.")
voices.security: the response unit: crisp, loud, procedural
voices.watcher: a person in the camera room, speaking into a handset: reports what the camera shows
voices.crowd: passers-by: startled, short, human; they never fight and are never used

pick.rule: variant index for the n-th use (0-based) of a key in a run: for i = 0..n, at = fnv1a32(seed + "|" + key + "|" + i) mod count, and if at equals the previous use's variant (count > 1) then at = (at + 1) mod count. fnv1a32 is the rulebook's (contracts/rules/rulebook.ref.ts, 32-bit FNV-1a over the UTF-16 code units). The key is event/verb/speaker/outcome/temperament/about with absent parts skipped; `seed` is the run's seed string. The line is the entry lookup() finds: every field an entry names must equal the query's, the entry naming the most fields wins, file order breaks a tie.

briefing.title: The Handover
card: Councillor Popovic has a file on us. Security gets it tonight.
At shift change he carries it out of the Civic Records Office.
We take him alive, get him into our getaway car and drive off.
Quietly, if we can. Others want him too, and this city notices noise.
We have $100,000, four people, and until 5:50, or 8:10 if we turn his driver.

page.rule: Brief 070 (Sky, 2026-10-26: the briefing as a full-screen page, modal until Begin; Glyph's mock briefs/070/glyph). Outside play, so the reading limits don't apply, but each way keeps to two sentences: its hint after the way's name (briefing.hints, the part after ': '), then `ways.<id>.line`. `when` is the plate beside the way's name, `target` the line under Vale's one fact (brief.json dossier.target), `ending` the line under the getaway car's still, `clock` the stations the page's clock shows (labels from briefing.timeline, unless `stations` words the mark for the page: Glyph R1 on 0.2.133, the 5:50 station is the short form, since the 5:20 station carries the condition; play's timeline keeps the full, true label), `cell` one line under each face, about this mission. `heads` the section heads (Glyph's mock; brief 070, Latch: the page showed none): `ways` keyed by how many ways the mission has (brief.json ways), so the head counts from the data; `where` over the plan, `clock` over the stations, `heat` beside the Heat word. `captions` a still's caption by its pin's place, where the target's name alone would not say where (Glyph N11 and R6: the pickup's words end at the service bay, so its still and legend name the service bay); other stills take targets.<key>.name. The target head stays less.briefing.target. Day and Night are off the page (Sky: night is not a toggle).
page.target: Comes out at 5:30 and leaves by car.

cards.rule: The feed's cards for engine events no scene covers (Sky's review 2026-10-16, messages.html §1 D). Each is a title and one result in the player's words with the engine's numbers, never the engine's sentence (its log keeps that). A card with `sight` in-sight shows only when an agent can see the place, as a city scene does; `sight` always shows wherever the cell stands (brief 067: the rival car turning in off Orbit Walk is heard, never seen), and its `at` then only says what the card points at. A result that is a record is chosen by the engine state `pick` names. {who} is the person or watcher as names.targets says it, {agent} "the Scout"; the host capitalises the first letter after filling. Brief 013 (takedowns): a card says only what the cell has seen or been told. Three kinds: (1) the cell's own acts (the agent is there, so no `sight`); (2) things at a place the cell may not be near: `sight` in-sight, and `at` names the engine position the check looks at (the log carries none; the host reads it from the game); (3) the city's answer to an Alert, which the Alert pill and the street show: a card says that it came and when, never who made the report or why. `needs` routine: a cause the cell can name only once a Watch has taught the person's routine (a missed check in); until then report.landed speaks alone. Codes the engine builds (stash.container, stash.door) are one card keyed by the prefix. A spoken line of an event shows with that event's card or scene, so it follows the same sight rule: a line is never shown when its card is hidden. Brief 014 (less reading): every card has a `fate`: beat (a one-line feed beat, `beat`; at most ten distinct lines in the file), icon (the street shows it: a marker, ring, lock or pip), alt (history only, behind L), debrief (the end says it). A card with no beat is never a card on screen; its title and result are the history lines. Brief 100 (Sky 2026-11-07, "explain why an alert raised, or why police came"): the cause of every Alert rise and police call now rides beside these cards, worded by the `why` block from the engine's alert history; a city's-answer card's own result still says only that it came (kind 3 above).

why.rule: Brief 100 (Sky 2026-11-07, playing: "It would be good to explain why an alert raised, or why police came"): the cause of every Alert rise and every police call, and the reporter while a report is still on its way, in the player's words, never the engine's sentence. The host reads the engine's alert history (Game.Ledger's alert rows today, keyed by the cause's first part; Keel's structured read to come: cause, who, what, where, when) and the log of the same tick. `alert` is keyed by the ledger cause: report:<kind> by its kind (seen, carry, dead, down, woken, noise, mark, missing, cut), report:<role> approach, report:office-staff staff, report:councillor let-go, then confirmed, gunfire, violence-seen violence, drawn-seen drawn, drawn-seen:people drawn-people, drawn-warned warned, takedown-fails fought, loiter, recorded, car-reported car, entry, sighting. `police` is keyed by what brought them, `onWay` by how a report travels. Each cause has a `title` (at most four words: its card and Journal row), a `short` (at most six words, lower case: the crucial card's dim line, followed by {where}, and the meter's row) and a `line` (one sentence: the Journal, Alt, the meter's hover, the debrief's timeline, brief 099). `again` follows a cause whose Alert came from the count of incidents (alert.byIncident: a second report means a search), and `effect` says what each Alert sets off. Fills: {who} the reporter or witness (a person as names.targets says them: the cast by name, a crowd person by job, crowd-<job>, else crowd; a watcher or unit as `by`; `by.another` when they share a job with {about}), {about} who or what it is about, {agent} the agent (the Scout), {where} the nearest of `places` within 13 m, else nearby, {to} `onWay.to`, {alert}, {clock} m:ss, {s} seconds, {cause} a cause's short. A cause the cell can't know yet uses its `unknown` variant (a check-in it hasn't watched). Not less.why, which is a hostile's fire cause. The city's answer cards keep their own results (brief 013); the why rides beside them.

onWay.rule: The marked reporter (brief 100, part 2): while a report is still to land, whoever makes it carries a `plate` (at most six words, then the seconds to its landing) and its `line` on Alt and in the Journal, by how it travels: radio (staff, from where they stand), walk or run (to the nearest report point, a staffed door or a call box: {to}), look (an Idealist checks the body first, so no landing yet), camera (on a watcher's tape: it lands at the desk's next scan), screen (a camera the Tech cut: the desk sees the dead screen at its next scan), robot (the patrol or the bin round rings the desk), checkin (a downed staff member's next mark, once their routine is known), tell (a call to a friend: no report, though a Loyal friend may make one). `fix` follows a plate the cell can still stop (a reporter downed first drops it), `nofix` one it can't (a tape, a dead screen, a robot's ring, a check-in). `stopped` is the pop when one never lands.

meter.rule: The Alert meter remembers (brief 100, part 3): a click or a hover on the Alert lamps lists each rise so far, newest first, each on two lines: `when` (the clock and the Alert it set) over `what` (its cause's short and where); a police call is listed the same way with `police` for its first line. `head` heads the list, `empty` shows at Alert 0 with nothing raised, `start` for an Alert set at the start. {where} is left out for a cause with no place (start, more, cordon, loud, split). Glyph lays it out; a row's hover is its cause's `line`.
meter.head: Why it's Alert {alert}

debrief.rule: Brief 096 (Sky 2026-11-04: "the End card needs to be plain english and clear but not too formal"): `cause` words the end card by the engine's reason, never one line per code: cause[Game.FailCode][key], the key FailCause.Why, except sealed (FailCause.Car: held, ready, empty, else unknown) and withdraw (its why). `head` is the title, `line` the sentence under it ({by} {agent} as less.failcam, {holders} as names.holders), and `story` names lines of `story` that follow "Popovic reached the getaway car." in the route, so the story runs to the end ({holders} is Game.CarHolders() at the end; a line with {holders} and none is left out). A cause with no entry (why unresolved) falls back to less.end.fail and briefing.fails. Once wired it replaces less.sealed.line, less.sealed.story and less.closedIn.line, which say the same. The end card in the player's words, by the ids of sim Debrief.cs (route, assets, investigation cause) and the engine's named-witness:<role>. A failure with a line in briefing.fails takes that line's first sentence as its headline and the whole line as its result; the Fixer's spoken fail or win line sits under it (events fail, win). An id with no sentence here is not shown. The replay verdict and hash are never player text. brief 014: the Standing line, one per district (rulebook debrief.lines.standing: district, from, to, band, cause, who). `line` is filled by the host from the debrief's fields: {district} is the district's name, {band} is bands[band], {from} and {to} are signed (+3, 0, -1), {cause} is causes[cause] filled with {who}, the person's name. The seen and found causes say what the city saw or found, with no name. The word causes are rumour, not fact the cell watched: they begin Word is, and name no face, place or time. `page`, brief 099 (Sky 2026-11-07: "that should be a like our book in terms of presentation, nice, visually appealing with explainers and stats"; "yeah, try A"): the debrief page's own words, concept A, the front page. The page also reads, unchanged: headline, result and cause (the outcome and its line), the start page's rows (book.job.needs.ways) with `how` and the time each came true, investigation and causes, assets (under city.kept), standing (the band and its cause under Standing), and the why block (an Alert rise's short under Alert; a row's hover is its line). Fills: {clock} m:ss, {op} an agent as the book's cell page names them (beside their face), {who} a person or camera as names.targets says them, {n} {trail} {alert} {missions} {guards} {cameras} {place} {by} {list} from the debrief and the ledger. Written through the style agent's short-line loop (Sky 2026-11-07: "sure"): Fable wrote, Motive scored 10/10; the runs are in runs/style-agent/short/.

rules.source: briefs/011/motive-fights.md §8 (Motive); words by Fable; each line fits Glyph's 110 characters
rules.one: One at a time, in priority order, lowest number first (H14, H16 and H15, the end steps, are -4 to -2: they win over every other hint, H17 and H13 included, when their trigger holds; their triggers never hold together; H20, Drive the car round (brief 059), is -7: it wins over H16 while the getaway car is still at the square, so the Take is not offered with a long carry ahead; H17, the fight hint, is -1, behind H15 so that Put Vale in the car wins while a fight holds the car, ahead of H13; H21 and H22, the control tips of brief 067, are -8 and -9: see `tips`).
rules.once: Each fires once per run, and H hides the layer for good.
rules.idle: A hint shows only after the cell has given no order for 8 s (H13's door cause, H21 and H22 show at once).
rules.tips: Brief 067 (Glyph, batch 0.2.123): H21 (Holster to stop firing: press F; engine 0.35 one input, Cease fire and X retired) and H22 (Scroll to switch) are control tips, not steps. Each teaches one input at the moment the player has just met the need for it, shows once, at once (no 8 s idle wait: that would hide it for the whole fight or the whole crowd), rings nothing (the lock reticle and the stack tab are already on screen), and retires for good when the input is used. They are -8 and -9, below every other hint's number, so they show the moment their trigger holds; the idle flavour hints and the end steps return after them. H21 teaches F as the way to stop firing (text.test.ts holds it to the game's own binding); the file no longer names X.
rules.vanishes: It vanishes the moment its gone-when act happens, or when its trigger stops holding.
rules.words: Each line names an agent, a verb and a target, introduces one verb, and never names an approach, a time or a sequence.
rules.short: Brief 014: the line at rest is `short` (one imperative, one [noun] ringed, no agent); this long line is Alt and the relearn key. See `less.hint` for when it shows and retires.

less.rule: brief 014 (Sky, 2026-10-16: "It's the reading, it's too much"). The play HUD at rest shows no sentences: people speaking (bubbles in the world), icons, numbers, rings, and at most two story beats. Every long line elsewhere in this file stays and is the Alt text (hold Alt, or the book's Journal) or the debrief; nothing was deleted. `fates` says where each group of text goes; the rest of this block is the short forms and the one-line price grammar. Told/learned holds: a beat or a pop never names what the cell has not been told or has not learned.

price.rule: One line per way: the verb, then only the fields that are not zero, always in `order`; an unknown number is "?". Money is compact ($90k, $1.5k, a range $40k–60k; under $1,000 as it is): the rows have fixed columns; the status pill and the debrief keep whole dollars. Locked rows show the same line dimmed. Alt shows every field including the zeros, and the rows a card carries today (`actions.*.does`, found, never found, wakes, seen by). No time and no chance (brief 101, Sky 2026-11-08: "Don't look at how long something takes because I don't have a choice with the action so it's irrelevant as a player. Only thing that feels time is important are the key events that happen"): a price is money, Trail, Alert risk and what the street will do, and never says how long the walk or the act takes, on the line or on Alt, nor a hit chance. A time stays only where the act opens a window in the world that the player plays to: the door a pressed call clears (`door`), a loop's run (`lasts`), the desk's report after a Disable (in `alert`).

On the hold pill, whose one line carries the target as well, the name is the verb's `withTarget` filled with the target's name from names.targets ("Listen to the guard", "Ask Inez", "Fire at a hostile"); a label and a name run together ("Listen the guard", Suture 2026-10-26) is a slip the checker now catches in the templates

feed.rule: The feed shows story beats only: a card's or a scene's `beat`, one short line each, and only when no bubble of that event's speech is on screen (say it where the player is looking: the person's own line if they are in view, else the beat). At most `maxOnScreen` at once, each gone after `seconds`, then it sits in the history (L). A beat identical to one shown in the last `dedupeSeconds` is dropped. A card with no `beat` is never on screen; its title and result are the history. The people in a scene speak as bubbles at the speaker: `bubblesAtOnce` at a time, `bubbleSeconds` each; overheard and approach scenes play every beat, call and city scenes their first `cityBeats`. A beat obeys the card's sight and needs rules (the cell is never told what it did not see).

It never explains and it is not a hint.

intel.rule: Brief 016 (Intel panel, Glyph's redesign). The tooltip of a fact slot on a person's card is one fragment of one or two words that only names the fact; the host decides whether the cell has learned or been told it (the slot's rim says which), so no word here says how it is known. A fragment is never a sentence, has no gendered word and never says who told it. `need`, `temperament` and `secret` are keyed by the value the cast and the rulebook carry (needs.rules.json kinds, people.rules.json temperaments and secrets.list); a new value without a fragment fails the test. Brief 017: `need` and `secret` hold one fallback word per KIND, shown only while the need or secret is told and not yet heard; after Listen the host shows the record's own `label` from contracts/people/<plan>.needs.json, so no record's name lives here. `{name}` is the lover's name as the HUD shows it elsewhere: the given name for named people, the word the plus the role for role-named ones (Inez, the guard). `verb` is the word on the chip and on an unknown slot: what would teach it.

done.rule: Brief 043 (the done moment; Sky 2026-10-22: it is not clear when a task has completed and what it gained). Labels and numbers, never sentences. The plate is the portrait plate's word for 2.2 s after a landing or a cancel, keyed by the engine's outcome (the last part of turn.<approach>.<outcome>) or `done`; kept reads as turned. The gain chip shows one icon-plus-word line per fact, at most three, and the facts a Watch or Listen teaches are Intel's own fragments (less.intel: the need's record label, the temperament, Loves {name}) so the chip and the Intel panel never disagree; only the words in `gain` are new. Brief 058 (Sky, 2026-10-25): a looped camera shows the desk a clean picture, so a loop is never "dark": `camera-looped` is the Loop chip (the 2:00 countdown rides the window marker), `camera-cut` the Disable chip, `camera-shot` the chip of a camera shot out, `parked` the chip of a car Drive that has arrived and `timetable` the chip of a Watch on the rival crew (brief 059: the street draws the three facts it teaches, the next move, the spring ring and the follow line, so the chip names them as one; a bare noun on the thing, as `rounds` is on the patrol). A window marker is an icon with a count or the doer's face; `close` is the pop on the thing when the window ends, by the marker's kind. Unlock-row pills are the verbs' own ring labels (actions.ring-*), shut ones struck through, so they carry no words here. Cancel: the tag before is `tag` or `tagCost`, the pop after `pop` or `popCost`, {verb} the ring label of the order dropped, {cost} one of `cost` by the engine's cancel cost (aborted, released, staff-report, vale-reports, ends; the rest are free and show no cost, and so is `lost` since brief 101: its word was the seconds the act had run, and no act's time shows in play, Sky 2026-11-08; `drives-on` is no cancel at all, engine 0.33.1: a Drive under way is refused `car-driving`, so Cancel is hidden for the driver and the riders and no tag or pop shows). Walking in: the plate shows `walk.plate` with {who} from `walk.who`; the pill and Alt show `walk.line` with {target} from names.targets and {verb} the ring label. The old 'serving a table, back in {s} s' refusal is retired (engine 0.23: the agent walks up to the server at the table). Focus (engine 0.35 one input, the sticky focus, GDD section 10): the plate under a focus that waits, two lowercase words by the engine's FocusOf state (aiming, walking-in, no-line, out-of-reach; firing shows no plate); no-line and out-of-reach say what the fire refusals say.

cars.rule: Brief 096, the lend (engine 0.42.0), placeholders for Fable: `goLent` the Go on Popovic's car once it is ours (its Go takes him out: the win is fixed, the mission runs on); `endWinHead` and `endWinLine` the end card's head and line after a win by that Go; `lentName` Popovic's car once it is ours (our own stays names.targets.car-getaway); the debrief's `carLost` (our car left standing at the end: +{trail} T, the police trace it) and `lentSeen` ({by} saw Popovic's car leave: +{trail} T and a lead, not a hunted car); `goClear` the Alt does-line of our car's Go once Popovic's car is ours (HudModel; was hard-coded). G1 (engine 0.43.0, rulebook car.go.waits; Latch), placeholders for Fable: a Go on either car while one of us is climbing in waits for him and goes the moment he is in. `goOnce` added to the Go row's line before the click ({list} who is climbing in), and its Alt does-line capitalised; `goWaiting` the Go row's line and Alt once given, until he is in; `goWaitsRoster` the climber's roster line under his portrait (after an arrow) while the Go waits for him.
cars.carLost: We left our car behind, and the police will trace it. Trail +{trail}.
cars.lentSeen: {by} saw Popovic's car leave: a lead, but not to our car. Trail +{trail}.
cars.endWinLine: We drove Popovic off in his own car.

police.rule: Brief 096, the lend (engine 0.42.0, Game.SplitPoliceAt), placeholders for Fable: the one countdown plate under the clock once Popovic is out. `head` with {time} (m:ss left), `why` the line under it, `left` who is still out ({list} their names, {n} how many), `clear` when nobody is, `end` the button that ends the mission now (End, in Withdraw's place; everyone not in a car that has left is captured).
police.head: Police close in {time}
police.why: Popovic is out. The rest get clear in our car.

tape.rule: Brief 096 (engine 0.40.0, bribes on camera), placeholders for Fable: the Pay or Pressure card's camera line, its eye's hover and the panel row. `seen` a camera the cell has watched would record it ({camera} its name, {alert} the Alert, {s} seconds until its desk sees it, {trail} the Trail); `maybe` one the cell hasn't watched; `loopEnds` added when a loop on it runs out inside the act ({t} the clock).
tape.seen: {camera} would tape it: Alert {alert} in {s} s, +{trail} T
tape.maybe: A camera might tape this: Watch {camera} to be sure

parked.rule: Brief 096 (engine 0.40.0, the parked car), placeholders for Fable: the Drive card's line where our car would stand on private ground. `seen` a watcher the cell knows would see it ({who} the watchers, {s} the seconds in sight before they report it); `maybe` one it doesn't know yet; `back` added while the patrol is rerouted ({t} when it is back).
parked.seen: Parked here, {who} would see it and report it in {s} s
parked.maybe: Parked here, {who} might see it: Watch first to be sure

crew.rule: Brief 096, placeholders for Fable (Latch; engine 0.41.0 rivals.turn): the cards of Watch, Listen, Pay and Mislead on a member of the rival crew on foot, and their feed footers. {usd} the Pay, {t} a clock, {who} the man. The lookout is named by his job (`lookout`); the others by names.holders.rival. `misled` and `misleadMissed` are the Mislead card's result (HostFeed; were hard-coded).
crew.watchDoes: Learn the crew's timetable: where each of them goes, and when.
crew.listenDoes: Hear whether he's in it for the money or loyal to his crew.
crew.payDoes: {usd} to walk away. A loyal man refuses and tells his crew.
crew.payDoesMercenary: He's in it for the money: he takes {usd} and walks off for good.
crew.payDoesLoyal: He's loyal: he refuses, tells his crew about the Fixer, and we keep the money.
crew.payUnknown: takes it, or refuses and tells his crew: Listen first
crew.payTakes: takes it and walks off for good
crew.payRefuses: refuses: his crew will know the Fixer
crew.misleadDoesLookout: Send him to watch the other door for a while. He comes back knowing the Scout's face.
crew.misleadDoesPosted: Send him to the lookout's post for a while. He comes back knowing the Scout's face.
crew.sees: He sees you coming and fires: come from behind
crew.armed: Armed: if he sees you coming, he fires
crew.heardMercenary: {who} is in it for the money.
crew.paid: {who} takes the money and walks off.
crew.refused: {who} won't take it, and tells his crew. The money stays with us.
crew.payMissed: {who} was gone before the Fixer paid. The money stays with us.
crew.misled: He takes the word and walks off. He'll be back.
crew.misleadMissed: The word missed him: he'd gone, or was already after Popovic's car.

pending.rule: Words drafted ahead of the engine (briefs 058 and 059, GDD v0.25.0). The host reads none of this. Each entry names its brief and says whether its code, key or trigger is a `guess`: the brief did not name it, and its owner confirms or renames it. When Keel lands a code or a verb, the entry moves unchanged to the section of the same name (locks, cards.items, events, dialogue, actions, activity, hints, less.price, targets) and Latch wires it in that batch; a `replaces` entry takes the place of the live one with the same key.  A test holds every line here to the live limits. Empty since the 059 port (2026-10-26): the Drive, the rival crew's Watch, the driver's tail fact, H16 and H20 are live.
